question: If not the risk you take, what did Benjamin Graham say should set the return you aim for?
answer: The intelligent effort you can and will put in. Graham rejected tying return to risk. A passive investor, wanting safety and no bother, should accept the minimum; more belongs to the alert one who works at it. A bargain found by research, he wrote, may carry less real risk than a bond.
move: Expect better results from more work, not from more risk.
simply: Two children want extra pocket money. One bets it on a coin toss; the other washes the neighbours’ cars. Only the second can count on being paid.
why: It changes what to do when you want more from your savings. Without the time or skill to research, the sensible choice is the simple, defensive route; reaching for riskier bets does not buy the extra return that only work can earn.
